character.effect_hint: The formula gives the new value and can use anything a rule formula can; its own name means the value so far (e.g. move_speed * 1.2), or replace it outright (e.g. str + agi). Several effects on one value run in turn: fixed entries first, then yours by Order (smallest first, 0 = first), then statuses. Order is required and must be unique on the sheet.
character.effect_hint_fixed: The formula gives the new value and can use anything a rule formula can; its own name means the value so far. Fixed entries run first, in the order defined; then players' effects (by their Order), then statuses.

b.names: Refer to fields, derived values and named formulas by name

d.basic: Roll three six-sided dice and add them
d.field: A number followed by d; the sides can be a field or a bracketed expression
d.keep: Roll 4d6 and keep the highest 3; lowest keeps the lowest
d.names: Between two names, put spaces around d (level dice with luck sides)
d.one: No count means one die; d% is d100
d.order: Dice come before * and /: this is (2d6) × 5

fn.clamp: Keep x between lo and hi
fn.highest: Roll n dice with s sides, add the highest k
fn.if: a if the condition holds, otherwise b
fn.lookup: Look a value up in one of the pack's tables
fn.lowest: Roll n dice with s sides, add the lowest k
fn.mod: Remainder of x / y (same sign as y)
fn.round: Round to nearest (.5 away from zero)
fn.sign: 1 if positive, -1 if negative, 0 if zero

fh.where: Dice work in a check's dice and in the keeper's ad-hoc checks and free rolls. Derived values, limits, initial values, targets and result conditions are recomputed every time, so they can't roll.

kp.action_hint: Write what your character does next ("I …"). It is parsed for you to confirm, with an estimate of how long it takes; you can resubmit until it starts. Once under way it can't be changed until it finishes or something interrupts it. Only confirmed actions change the world.
kp.busy: Your action is still under way. You'll be told when it finishes or something affects you; until then it can't be changed.
kp.chat_hint: Ask questions and clarify. The keeper answers only what your character could know; nothing here counts as an action.
kp.confirm_hint: Once confirmed, the time can't be changed.
kp.unresolved: These references could not be matched; use @ and parse again:

play.map_hint: Tap a person or place to @ it; tap the ground to pick a destination. Describe height in words ("the rooftop", "100 m up").

review.not_in_review: This round is not awaiting review; read only.

cls_help.player: Player-defined: entered by the player during character creation.
cls_help.runtime: Runtime: changes during play (e.g. current HP); players can't set it, only the keeper's rulings change it. Needs an initial value.

rules.derived_hint: Numbers computed by formula from other fields; players can't enter them. The three below are required by the engine: keep their names, but write their formulas.
rules.editing: Editing {id} v{version}; saving creates a new version.
rules.fields_hint: Values and text on the sheet. The appearance field is required: other players' handles for this character are generated from it.

g.effects: Entries may carry effects (modify derived values)
g.fields_hint: Every entry has a name and a description; add any numbers each entry needs here, such as rank or cost. Leave empty if none.
g.hidden: Hide the whole group from players
g.label: Group name (shown to players)
g.name: Group ID (internal code)
g.presets_hint: Entries written into the rules that players don't fill in. When the condition is true the entry appears on the sheet and its effects apply; otherwise it doesn't appear. Conditions may only use this sheet's fields; text values need double quotes, e.g. class = "warrior", class != "warrior" or and(class = "warrior", str >= 3). Fixed entries don't count toward the min/max above.
g.shapes: Area shapes entries may have (for area attacks, beams…; leave all unticked if unused)

rules.groups_hint: A group is one kind of entry on the sheet, such as class skills, personal skills or special abilities; make one group per kind. Each entry under it is one specific skill or ability. Entries come from two places: players add their own when creating a character, and you can write fixed entries here (optionally with a condition, e.g. only for one class).

help.appearance: Appearance: the player describes how the character looks. When others first see the character, its handle (e.g. "woman in a red scarf") is generated from this. It can't be removed or retyped.
help.can_fly: Can fly: ticked by the player, off by default. Flyers travel in a straight line at fly speed; others go up or down first and then along the ground at move speed. It can't be removed or retyped.
help.concealment: Multiplies how far others can notice this character: 1 is normal, 0.3 means others must be much closer. The default 1 is fine.
help.fly_multiplier: How many times the move speed a flyer flies. Default 1. Only matters for characters who can fly.
help.fly_speed: Metres per minute when flying; default fly_multiplier * move_speed. Only matters for characters who can fly.
help.hear_distance: How far (in metres) this character hears people talking. Bystanders within this range of either speaker hear the whole conversation, relayed by the keeper. Required, e.g. 30 * hear_multiplier. Walls are ignored.
help.hear_multiplier: Hearing multiplier, default 1. Skills and statuses can modify it (e.g. keen ears ×2); use it in the hearing range formula.
help.move_speed: Metres per minute. Required, e.g. 80 for an ordinary person, or 60 + agi * 2.
help.perception_radius: How far (in metres) this character notices others. Required, e.g. 50 + per, or a constant like 100.

kind_help.boolean: Yes/no: a checkbox, e.g. can fly. It's 1 or 0 in formulas.
kind_help.resource: Resource: a value with a ceiling that gets spent or restored (HP, mana, uses left). A maximum is required and may be a formula such as hp_max.
kind_help.text: Text: descriptions such as background; with choices, the player picks one of them.

rules.levels_hint: Checked in order; the first true condition wins. Variables: roll, target, difficulty, opp_roll, opp_target.
rules.locked: Required by the engine; can't be changed

ph.choices: e.g. red, blue, green (comma-separated; leave empty for free text)

rules.player_entities: Entities each player creates (template, min, max)
rules.problems: {n} problems; can't save a version yet (drafts are always fine)
rules.rules_text: Rules text (free text for the keeper)
rules.samples_hint: Checked on save: every example must produce the expected derived values.
rules.tables_hint: One row per line: key,value. Range tables take the largest key not above the input; exact tables need an exact match.
rules.template_hint: A template is the format of one kind of character sheet, not a specific character: players fill a sheet from it. One template is enough if every player has the same kind of sheet; add a second if each player also controls, say, a companion. The ID is an internal code (lowercase letters, digits, underscores, e.g. hero); the label is what players see. The default character works as is.
rules.unsaved: Unsaved changes; a draft is saved automatically

state.patch_hint: Edits are validated like adjudications and logged as admin overrides.

talk.hint: Talking happens face to face and is heard at once. While any conversation is open the round won't resolve; talking takes no game time.
talk.invited_me: @{label} wants to talk to you. If you accept, what you were doing stops and you'll act again after the talk.
talk.none: No conversation. Use Talk next to someone in the map tab's “Currently perceived” list.
